Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.snap

Class WindowSnap3D

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.snap.WindowSnap3D
public final class WindowSnap3D extends Object
The pure world-space geometry of window snapping on the native 3D desktop: the Frame3D counterpart of the 2D/Swing desktop's SnappingDesktopManager, reduced to float arithmetic so it is headless-testable.

The zone vocabulary and the half/maximise target rule are not re-invented here: they are the shared WindowSnap model the 2D desktop already uses, reached through its float zoneForRect/ boundsForRect overloads. What is 3D-specific is only the coordinate plumbing — a dragged window is a centre translation plus a preferred size times a uniform scale in a y-up world space whose origin is the screen centre, and the usable region is the screen minus the taskbar's reserved strips and the title-bar headroom the decoration's maximise already leaves.

Snapping is edge-based rather than pointer-based: a window snaps when its own left/right/top edge comes within DEFAULT_EDGE_THRESHOLD of the matching screen edge while it is being dragged, which is the natural gesture when the whole window (not just a title bar) follows the pointer.

  • Field Details

    • DEFAULT_EDGE_THRESHOLD

      public static final float DEFAULT_EDGE_THRESHOLD
      How close, in world units, a dragged window's edge must come to a screen edge to snap. The screen is ~0.36 world units wide for a 1920 px display, so this is on the order of sixty pixels: easy to hit by dragging to the edge without snapping on ordinary moves.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FIT_MARGIN

      public static final float FIT_MARGIN
      Shrink factor applied to the aspect-preserving fit of a pure-3D window into its snap target, so a snapped window keeps a visible margin instead of touching its neighbours. Matches the decoration's maximise margin.

    • HEADROOM
